Cash runway has fallen to {{fact:0876a4c5-62e5-4171-8850-2564f739afc2}} months, so the borrower's time to reach profitability or raise new funding is getting short. The steadily falling runway and cash covenant headroom show this is a sustained trend, not a one-off. Revenue tracking ahead of plan suggests the pressure comes from cash burn rather than weak sales.

Headroom on the minimum runway covenant has shrunk each month, from {{fact:85e42179-b128-45b9-8622-58c083af9a0e}} in August to {{fact:817703a5-ed3c-49e1-b9c0-55b878918d35}} in October. Runway of {{fact:5e075111-4594-4eda-9eeb-b1d483aab321}} months is still above the {{fact:caaa8855-1488-43ab-a0d9-d277f5ee9bea}}-month floor, but if the decline continues at this pace, the cushion would be gone within a few months.

Unrestricted cash headroom fell from {{fact:62e6d8fc-98c7-419b-9206-889afb0aa3f4}} in August to {{fact:71bf8060-93da-4884-a4a3-fae49d106867}} in October. Cash of {{fact:1300f6f3-f9f0-4192-86c7-2b2024c61b06}} still clears the {{fact:f59c1e75-ca5d-4e05-a55c-f4d06b43784c}} minimum. The falling cash balance is the root of the shrinking runway, so this signal and the runway signals describe the same burn.

This headroom is essentially flat, moving only from {{fact:973da0b7-3049-49dd-b547-9f41cace8037}} to {{fact:83a42716-5b75-41e8-a15f-2e31b29bc907}}. Revenue is running at {{fact:c113aae2-3896-4363-909b-a6c665eb7f7c}} of plan against an {{fact:c19644d5-7664-4763-b0b6-a0c4ceb67a4d}} floor. This is a mitigating point: it suggests the cash decline is not caused by a revenue shortfall.
